evidence: AC: 'crown-jewels rotated and external trust updated'
Scope adjustment: 'rotate ONLY secrets that can be regenerated internally in this session, and flag third-party or externally anchored credentials'
'Externally anchored secrets are tracked in follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler ... intentionally not blockers for this ticket's close'
findings.finding: Acceptance Criterion 'Every migrated secret re-seeded/rotated; crown-jewels rotated and external trust updated' contradicts the Completion Scope Adjustment, which narrows autonomous rotation to internally-regenerable secrets and defers externally-anchored crown-jewels (Anthropic API key, Gerrit admin password, jira-api-token) to follow-up 'auspicial-wily-warbler'. scenarios: Executor reads AC literally, blocks close until Anthropic/Gerrit/Jira trust is updated — contradicting the narrowed scope
Reviewer cannot tell whether 'crown-jewels rotated' AC is satisfied at close
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite AC to: 'Internally-regenerable secrets rotated this session; externally-anchored crown-jewels flagged to auspicial-wily-warbler (not a close blocker)'.

scenarios: An EC2 instance boots (or a consumer re-materializes secrets) after the apply-reset but before the deferred externally-anchored secrets are rotated by the warbler follow-up — the CHANGEME fail-fast aborts the boot / abort fetch
Operator closes this ticket believing the window is safe while most slots sit at CHANGEME awaiting a separate human-coordinated ticket

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit back-out/rollback for the CHANGEME reset window (e.g. capture current secret values to a secure ephemeral store before the apply, or sequence rotation per-slot so services never simultaneously depend on CHANGEME) and state the abort criteria.
evidence: Step 1: 'RESETS each live seeded secret to the placeholder'
Verification: 'write a names-only SSM parameter snapshot ... never values'
Step 4: 'Permanently delete the affected object versions'
No stated rollback/back-out if rotation fails mid-window
findings.finding: Step 1 resets every live seeded secret to the CHANGEME placeholder in a single window, relying on Step 2 rotation to restore working values, yet the Verification section mandates a NAMES-ONLY snapshot ('never values'). There is therefore no captured-value restore path: if the Step 2 rotation fails partway through the maintenance window, all affected prod secrets are stuck at CHANGEME with no back-out, and the destructive state-version deletion (Step 4) is irreversible by design.
scenarios: Rotation of secret N fails after secrets 1..N-1 already reset to CHANGEME — dependent services fail-fast and stay down with no restore path
Operator must abort the window but cannot restore prior working secret values
findings.suggested_fix: Before Step 1, securely export current values (out-of-band, not to state) so any slot can be restored; or rotate each slot immediately after its reset rather than resetting all slots first.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a resumable, per-secret rotation ledger (names only) so a partially-completed rotation can be resumed idempotently — track each slot's rotated/pending status and re-run put-parameter --overwrite only for pending slots.
evidence: Step 2: 'In the SAME maintenance window, re-seed/ROTATE every affected secret'
Verification captures only a 'names-only SSM parameter snapshot' before surgery, not a per-secret rotated/not-rotated status that would let a resumed run skip completed slots
ABSENCE: no idempotency/resume guidance for a partially completed rotation across ~22+4 slots, though put-parameter --overwrite is itself idempotent per-slot
findings.finding: The multi-secret rotation loop ('re-seed/ROTATE every affected secret') is not specified as resumable/idempotent: if the maintenance-window session is interrupted mid-rotation, the plan provides no per-secret progress tracking to distinguish rotated slots from those still sitting at the CHANGEME placeholder.
findings.location: Step 2 (re-seed/ROTATE every affected secret) and Verification (names-only snapshot bullet)
scenarios: Session aborts after rotating 10 of 22 secrets; on resume it is unclear which slots remain at CHANGEME and would fail user_data.sh fail-fast

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency-control and ordering between this apply, the 'rubied' apply, and the historical-version scrub (state-lock ownership, which apply runs first, and that the scrub runs AFTER all writers quiesce) so neither apply races the shared tfstate nor lets rubied-written versions escape the purge.
evidence: 'Coordinate with the SEPARATE "rubied" apply that is seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params so the state scrub covers those params too'
Two terraform applies against s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate contend for the same backend; the plan names no state-lock (e.g. DynamoDB lock) or apply ordering
Step 4 permanently deletes object versions while rubied writes new versions — a TOCTOU where the scrub can miss versions rubied writes after the snapshot, or delete/interleave versions mid-apply
findings.finding: The plan mutates shared remote tfstate and the shared /rebar/prod/ SSM namespace concurrently with the SEPARATE 'rubied' apply, but never states the concurrency-control / ordering that prevents the two terraform applies from racing the same backend state or the historical-version scrub from racing rubied's writes.
scenarios: rubied's apply and this apply both hold/contend the tfstate lock, one fails or corrupts state
the scrub enumerates versions, then rubied writes a fresh cleartext version that survives the purge — the exposure the ticket exists to remediate persists undetected
findings.suggested_fix: Add an ordering clause: rubied applies first (or serialize both under the tfstate DynamoDB lock), confirm both applies are complete and no further writers are pending, THEN enumerate-and-purge historical versions; re-snapshot version IDs immediately before deletion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the rubied coordination as an explicit ordering/precondition: assert rubied's 4 new MCP-PAT params are declared write-only (value_wo) per ADR 0105, and require the scrub (Step 4) to run only AFTER rubied's state-mutating writes are complete, enumerating any version rubied produced.
evidence: Plan: 'Coordinate with the SEPARATE "rubied" apply that is seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params so the state scrub covers those params too (they are also SecureString secrets under /rebar/prod/).'
The scrub (Step 4) permanently deletes retained object versions; a rubied apply that writes state AFTER the scrub reintroduces a version the scrub already cleared
ADR 0105 requires new SecureString secrets be value_wo; if rubied's params used the old value=/ignore_changes contract they would land cleartext in state
findings.finding: The rubied coordination states that the scrub should cover rubied's new MCP-PAT params but does not specify the ordering/atomicity constraint that makes coverage correct — rubied's params must be write-only (value_wo) AND any rubied cleartext-producing state write must complete before this ticket's scrub, else a rubied write lands a fresh cleartext state version after the scrub runs.
findings.location: Coordination section / AC 'rubied MCP-PAT params covered by the same scrub'
scenarios: rubied applies (or refreshes) after this ticket's Step 4 scrub, writing a new terraform.tfstate version; if rubied's params are not write-only, that version carries cleartext and survives the scrub
The two applies interleave and each produces state versions the other's scrub does not enumerate

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit safeguard to the state-scrub step: enumerate the exact historical version-ids to delete (dry-run listing recorded to the session artifact), assert the CURRENT/latest tfstate version is EXCLUDED and verified clean before any deletion, and note the DATA LOSS RISK that deleting the current version destroys live state with no back-out.
evidence: Step 4: 'Permanently delete the affected object versions (or roll the bucket / lifecycle-expire old versions ...)'
Runbook §Back-out: 'There is no back-out for the one-time state scrub or the secret rotation'
The plan enumerates deletion but never asserts the CURRENT (latest) tfstate object version is explicitly excluded from the delete set, nor requires a dry-run listing to be confirmed before deletion
ABSENCE: no rollback/recovery path and no invariant that a clean current state exists and is preserved before destroying prior versions
findings.finding: The permanent deletion of retained tfstate object versions (step 4 / VERIFICATION) is an irreversible destructive operation on the persisted state store with no back-out and no safeguard ensuring the CURRENT/live tfstate version is preserved. If the wrong version — or the current version — is deleted, live infrastructure state tracking is destroyed with no recovery path.
findings.location: Steps §4 (SCRUB the historical cleartext) and Verification (final bullet); runbook §REMEDIATE step 4 / §Back-out
scenarios: Operator runs delete-object --version-id against the wrong version-id and removes the live state pointer
A scripted loop over list-object-versions accidentally includes the current version marker
findings.suggested_fix: Before deletion, capture `aws s3api list-object-versions` output, mark the IsLatest=true version as never-delete, confirm the live state is already scrubbed (value:null) on that latest version, then delete only the enumerated older version-ids; record version-ids in the artifact.
